Input x goes through fixed W and, in parallel, through A to a narrow width r, then B back to the output width; only the latter route is scaled by alpha/r before addition. The diagram’s output is Wx+(alpha/r)BAx. For four inputs and three outputs, rank 2 gives A=2*4=8 and B=3*2=6, so 14 entries can change, with alpha/r=2/2=1. The one-row input contains four ones and its output-square mean is a loss that aims at zero. The current text now names SGD as the update method, states that backward computes gradients, and states that step updates the selected parameters with learning rate 0.1. Independent old tensor copies support the exact unchanged-W and changed-B comparisons. The exercise changes rank and alpha together to 1, keeping scale 1 and reducing the count to 4+3=7; neither the smaller count nor this one update measures image/text task quality. The full-model paragraph locates rank-8/alpha-16 corrections in q/v transformations (scale 2), keeps the visual base and now explicitly named speech recognizer ASR untrained by this step, and separates the 0.00003 full-model learning rate from the small 0.1 example. It reports 1,605,632 trainable entries, 0.0754% of the adapted model, a 6.44 MB correction-only file and 112 parameter tensors, while limiting base invariance evidence to sampled positions. Those are a cited prior experiment, not a run I reproduced. After fully rereading this text and all four necessary linked prerequisites, and viewing all three figures again, I found no remaining obstacle to explaining or checking the example.

necessary_prerequisites.current_reader_summary: LoRA preserves W and adds a narrow A-then-B route. The 16-to-2-to-12 example requires 56 trainable entries, not replacement of the original 192 weights; its original bias also stays frozen. B starts at zero, making the initial output equal to the base and the first A gradient zero while B can have a nonzero gradient. Query and Value are described as feature transformations, supplying enough context for q/v names in 20.6. The cited style results separate reduced parameter counts from answer correctness.

The project uses delta W=(alpha/rank)BA. Doubling alpha doubles only the correction when A/B/rank stay fixed, and floating residuals are allowed by allclose. Changing rank also changes matrix shapes, so it cannot alone imply a final correction is halved. A numerical fingerprint is an identifier derived from parameter values in a fixed order.

The gradient measures local sensitivity of loss to each adjustable value. backward computes those sensitivities; it does not itself change the parameter. A learning-rate update subtracts a scaled gradient, as 1-0.1*(-4)=1.4 demonstrates. This makes the revised backward/step sentence understandable.

A tensor groups numbers along axes; scalar, vector and matrix are different shapes. The table and its mean examples make rows/columns and shape concrete. Thus 112 correction tensors are 112 grouped parameter containers, distinct from 1,605,632 individual entries.
